headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage: Authelia can egress broadly while the companion list has no runtime surfaces, so the pair’s main hazards are indirect and configuration-dependent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible default injection channel is documented between Authelia and awesome-production-machine-learning. Authelia exposes OIDC/ForwardAuth and broad egress, but the list has no runtime I/O surfaces or execution path, so there is no agent-to-agent instruction bridge in the profiles.
conditions: IF the list is embedded into a shared filesystem or clipboard workflow with Authelia outputs, injection risk becomes possible.
IF an orchestrator parses Authelia-generated text as instructions for another agent, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the list read-only and outside any shared workspace.
Disable copy-paste handoff between the two agents.
Require explicit human review before any Authelia output is reused as instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to all inter-agent text transfers.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and can handle OIDC/ForwardAuth traffic, so sensitive identity data could leave the local boundary if it is configured to process it. The awesome list has no data-touching surfaces, so leakage is one-way and indirect rather than mutual.
conditions: IF Authelia is pointed at sensitive identity or session data, that data can traverse network boundaries.
IF the list is used as a source of copied configuration snippets containing secrets, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Review Authelia upstream/downstream data flows before deployment.
Avoid placing secrets in any text copied into the list workflow.
Restrict Authelia egress to approved endpoints.
Use a separate workspace for documentation and runtime configs.
requires-engineering: add DLP or redaction on Authelia logs and outputs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: The profiles do not show overlapping write surfaces or shared mutable resources. Authelia is not runnable here and only exposes API-style interfaces, while the awesome list has no runtime capabilities, so there is no documented write-write conflict.
conditions: IF both are later deployed against the same writable directory or OAuth resource, conflict risk would need reevaluation.
mitigations: Keep the list non-executable and read-only.
Do not mount Authelia and documentation into the same writable path.
Recheck permissions before any shared deployment.
requires-engineering: introduce locking if a shared mutable backend is added.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can emit authentication-related outputs, but the awesome list has no action-taking or parsing behavior documented, so there is no default chain where B blindly acts on A. The interaction is therefore not evidenced and appears limited to manual reuse.
conditions: IF a downstream system copies Authelia output into another agent without verification, cascading errors become plausible.
IF the list is repurposed into an automated pipeline, the risk increases.
mitigations: Require human verification of any Authelia-derived claims.
Do not automate from the list into production actions.
Label Authelia outputs as untrusted until checked.
requires-engineering: add schema validation before downstream consumption.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is documented. Authelia and the awesome list touch no declared regulated data classes, and there is no evidence of residency, retention, or certification conflict in the profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is later used with regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII, compliance must be reassessed.
mitigations: Document the data classes before deployment.
Keep regulated data out of the pair until reviewed.
Add a retention policy if logs are introduced.
requires-engineering: perform a formal compliance review for any regulated workload.
